title: Determination of the critical values of flow parameters characteristic of the alignment of cylindrical nano-objects in suspensions
author: Loshkarev, Vlasova, et al.
materials: Due to the flexibility of the silicon rubber tube, the transmitter can move relative to the receiver during the measurements. As a result, the cross-section of the channel in the measurement zone represents a flattened circle with the width b corresponding to the gap between the transmitter and the receiver. The cross-section of the rest part of the channel has a circular shape. The thermostat being a part of the setup makes it possible to maintain the temperature of the suspension in the range from 29 to 31 °С.

steps.title: Prepare carbon nanofiber suspension
steps.instruction: Subject the aqueous colloid of carbon nanofibers Palizh‑100 (≈3.8 wt %) to intense sonication at 100 W acoustic power for 40 min, then centrifuge at 5 000–7 000 g for 10–30 min using a high‑speed centrifuge to remove large agglomerates; keep the resulting stable suspension for acoustic measurements.

steps.title: Assemble and condition measurement cell
steps.instruction: Connect the silicon‑rubber tube measurement cell (cruciform with four branch pipes) to the closed‑loop circular channel of inner diameter D on two branches, and plug the transmitter (T) and receiver (R) on the other two so that their end faces lie on the inner wall of the channel; install the peristaltic pump with adjustable speed, and set the thermostat to maintain the suspension temperature between 29 °C and 31 °C.

steps.title: Set flow constriction degree above alignment threshold
steps.instruction: Adjust the gap width b between transmitter and receiver to obtain a constricted cross‑section Sg such that the flow constriction degree Z = S0/Sg = D² b (1 − b²/D)⁻¹ is greater than 2.5 (the theoretical minimum for perfect alignment).

steps.title: Determine critical flow speed Vcr
steps.instruction: With Z fixed at the value set above, vary the peristaltic‑pump speed to produce a series of flow speeds V in the round‑section (cross‑section S0); for each V record the acoustic attenuation spectrum and calculate the longitudinal viscosity η(V); continue until η approaches a limiting value η∞ (e.g., ≈5.2 mPa·s) and the η(V) curve shows only a slight slope (typically V > 4 mm s⁻¹). Identify Vcr as the lowest V at which |η − η∞| ≤ 5 % of η∞.

steps.title: Determine critical constriction Zcr
steps.instruction: Set the flow speed to a value just above Vcr (e.g., V ≈ 4.5 mm s⁻¹). Vary the gap width b to change Z over a wide range (e.g., Z = 1.16 – 16.25). For each Z record the acoustic attenuation spectrum and compute η(Z). Identify Zcr as the smallest Z at which |η − η∞| ≤ 5 % of η∞ (experimentally ≈1.6).

steps.title: Confirm laminar flow regime
steps.instruction: Calculate the Reynolds number for each experimental condition; ensure it does not exceed 80 to guarantee laminar flow and avoid turbulence effects.

steps.title: Report critical flow parameters
steps.instruction: Report the determined critical flow speed Vcr (≈4.5 mm s⁻¹) and critical constriction degree Zcr (≈1.6) as the values beyond which cylindrical nano‑objects align parallel to the flow direction.
